title: Determination of Total Soluble Sugars in Pteridophytes Using the Anthrone Method
author: Denova‐Lozano, Chamorro‐Flores, et al.

steps.title: Extract fresh plant tissue
steps.instruction: Collect fresh leaf sections from the middle portion of each pteridophyte species (Selaginella pallescens, Selaginella sartorii, Pleopeltis madrensis, Pleopeltis polylepis var. polylepis), using three biological replicates per species and ensuring equal sample weights, then extract the tissues with 80% ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare anthrone reagent
steps.instruction: Immediately before use, prepare the anthrone working reagent by carefully diluting concentrated sulfuric acid, then dissolving anthrone in the diluted acid; protect the reagent from light and store it under appropriate conditions to maintain stability.

substeps.instruction: Dilute concentrated H₂SO₄ according to the required working concentration (exact dilution not specified).
Dissolve anthrone in the diluted sulfuric acid to obtain the working reagent.
Prepare the reagent fresh, keep it protected from light, and store it under recommended conditions.

steps.title: Create glucose standard curve
steps.instruction: Prepare a glucose stock solution and generate a series of controlled dilutions using sterile materials and careful pipetting to construct a standard curve for quantifying total soluble sugars.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a glucose stock solution (concentration not specified).
Perform a series of serial dilutions of the stock solution with sterile water or buffer to obtain standards covering the desired concentration range.
Use precise pipetting techniques for each dilution to ensure reproducibility.
